subject: Megacorp SLA redlines and latency carveouts
messages:
From: Diane Huang <diane.huang@megacorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@megacorp.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood SLA — request for uptime/latency clarifications and credit scope

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the draft SLA and have three primary asks before we can move to an internal approval: 1) clarify monthly credit calculation when availability drops below 99.95% (our standard is 99.99%), 2) explicit latency SLOs for p95/p99 and how those factor into credits, and 3) carveouts for planned maintenance windows and cloud provider incidents.

We attached the redlines from our side as a starting point (see Redwood_SLA_EditProposals.xlsx). For context, Megacorp runs customer-facing features where a sustained p99 > 800ms could materially impact our SLAs to our customers, so we need clear remedies.

Can your legal/sales ops propose a version that keeps Redwood's availability guarantees but narrows the credit exposure? Timeline: our procurement deadline is 2026-10-12.

Best,
Diane
Diane Huang
Head of Platform Reliability, Megacorp
[Attachment: Redwood_SLA_EditProposals.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Huang <diane.huang@megacorp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA — request for uptime/latency clarifications and credit scope

Hi Diane — really appreciate the clear asks and the spreadsheet. Quick read through and a proposed middle-ground below. Please see the attached annotated SLA (Redwood_SLA_Template_v1.2.pdf) for line references.

Summary of our proposal (high level):
- Availability baseline: maintain 99.95% as our standard production uptime for hosted customers.
- Credit bands: introduce graduated monthly credits capped at 50% of the monthly invoice. Example: 99.95–99.8% = 5% credit; 99.8–99.0% = 15% credit; <99.0% = 50% credit.
- Latency SLOs: publish p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 750ms for requests routed to our lowest-latency cluster. Credits tied only to sustained latency regressions that are reproducible by our test harness over a 6-hour window, and after on-call confirms incident classification.
- Maintenance carveouts: planned maintenance windows (advertised 72 hours in advance to the contact list) are excluded from credit calculations if scheduled during off-peak hours. Emergency cloud provider outages will be excluded if we can show provider incident report and cross-region failover attempts.

Operational asks from Megacorp:
- 30-day notice before large rollouts that change model families or quantization profiles so we can run regression checks.
- Access to an agreed synthetic test endpoint for monitoring p95/p99 (read-only) so Megacorp can correlate observability.

Next steps I propose: Ben and Laura will tighten the credit cap language and the exact mathematical definition in the SLA, and then we can produce a single tracked copy for signature. Can you confirm Megacorp is flexible on the 50% cap and the 6-hour reproducibility window?

Thanks — sending annotated SLA now.

Regards,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Template_v1.2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diane Huang <diane.huang@megacorp.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA — request for uptime/latency clarifications and credit scope

Diane — looping in Laura and Karthik for legal/ops detail. A couple of practical changes from our side after reviewing with Commercial Ops:

1) Credit cap tweak: we can move the cap to 40% of monthly invoice for the first 12 months of the contract, then revert to 50% thereafter. That gives Megacorp a stronger immediate protection while capping our initial exposure.
2) Latency definition: p99 credits will only trigger if p99 exceeds 900ms for a rolling 6-hour window AND total error-rate attributable to Redwood services is <0.1% (to avoid double-counting provider errors).
3) Maintenance scheduling: clarify "off-peak" as 01:00–05:00 PT for Megacorp's primary region, and require an internal rollback playbook be provided (staggered rollout recommended).

Laura — can you produce a short clause (two paragraphs) that captures the reproducibility test (what logs/trace data we need to confirm latency regression) and the coordination steps for cloud provider incidents? Karthik, please prepare a short operational checklist Megacorp can use during cutover.

Diane — are these acceptable? If yes, we'll incorporate and push a tracked draft by EOD 10/07.

Thanks,
Ben
VP, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Diane Huang <diane.huang@megacorp.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@megacorp.com
Date: Fri, 08 Oct 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA — request for uptime/latency clarifications and credit scope

Thanks Priyom and Ben — this is helpful. Megacorp can accept:
- Availability baseline at 99.95% with the proposed graduated credits, pending final legal language on cap timing;
- Latency carveout language provided the p99 trigger is capped at 900ms and you provide the reproducibility checklist and read-only synthetic endpoint;
- Maintenance carveouts as defined (we will align on the rollback playbook).

We are OK with the 40% initial cap for 12 months. Procurement will need the final tracked SLA by 2026-10-12 with a DocuSign link for signature. Please attach the final draft and a short summary of any monitoring endpoints we can add to our internal runbooks.

Diane
Diane Huang
Head of Platform Reliability, Megacorp
[Reference: Megacorp procurement deadline 2026-10-12]
